Operator:
Good day and thank you for standing by. Welcome to the StellarTech Q2 Earnings Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a Q&A session. Today's call is being recorded.
I would now like to hand the call over to Jane Smith, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Jane Smith, VP of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, and welcome to StellarTech’s Q2 earnings call. Joining me today are Alex Johnson, CEO; Michael Lee, CFO; and Sarah Chen, Chief Technology Officer.
Earlier today, we published our earnings press release and presentation, which are available on our Investor Relations site. Today’s discussion may include forward-looking statements. With that, let me turn the call over to Alex Johnson.

Alex Johnson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thanks, Jane, and welcome everyone.

We’re pleased with our performance this quarter. I want to highlight a few areas. Okay, here's a detailed breakdown of the Q1 revenue performance, incorporating the provided summary and adding plausible, fictional data and analysis to create a realistic financial narrative:

Good morning, everyone. Today, I'll be providing a detailed analysis of our Q1 2024 revenue performance. We're pleased to report a strong start to the year, with total revenue reaching KRW 65.4 trillion, marking a new all-time high for a first quarter. This reflects a continuation of the positive trends we observed in late 2023 and underscores the effectiveness of our strategic initiatives.

Key Highlights:

*   Total Revenue: KRW 65.4 trillion
*   Quarter-over-Quarter (QoQ) Growth: 6.2%
*   Year-over-Year (YoY) Growth: 18.2%

The 6.2% QoQ increase is particularly noteworthy, especially considering the typical seasonal slowdown experienced in the consumer electronics sector during Q1 following the holiday season. This performance is primarily attributed to strong smartphone sales, up 8% QoQ. Our flagship Galaxy S24 series, launched in late January, experienced exceptional demand. Pre-orders exceeded internal projections by 25%, driven by innovative features like enhanced AI-powered camera capabilities and improved battery life. Specifically, the Galaxy S24 Ultra model saw a 30% increase in sales volume compared to its predecessor, the S23 Ultra, in the same launch period last year. We estimate this contributed an additional KRW 2.8 trillion in revenue compared to the previous quarter. This was also aided by targeted marketing campaigns emphasizing the device's advanced features and user-friendly interface, resulting in a higher conversion rate among potential customers.

While overall TV unit sales were flat QoQ, we observed a shift towards higher-end models, particularly our OLED and Neo QLED ranges. This resulted in a higher average selling price (ASP) for TVs, mitigating the impact of lower unit sales. Specifically, ASP increased by 5% QoQ, driven by strong demand for our 77-inch and larger screen sizes. This trend towards larger, premium TVs indicates a growing preference for immersive home entertainment experiences. Our digital appliance division continued its growth trajectory, driven by increased demand for energy-efficient and smart home appliances. In particular, our Bespoke line of refrigerators and washing machines saw strong adoption, especially in the North American and European markets. We estimate that the introduction of our new AI-powered washing machine, which optimizes washing cycles based on fabric type and stain level, contributed an additional KRW 350 billion to the division's revenue.

The impressive 18.2% YoY growth is a testament to our strategic focus on innovation, product differentiation, and market expansion. Key factors contributing to this growth include robust growth in smartphones, up 22% YoY. This segment was the primary driver of YoY revenue growth, fueled by the aforementioned success of the Galaxy S24 series and the sustained popularity of our mid-range A-series devices. We saw particularly strong growth in emerging markets, such as India and Southeast Asia, where our A-series smartphones offer a compelling combination of features and affordability. We estimate that our market share in India increased by 2 percentage points YoY, reaching 26%, driven by the aggressive marketing and distribution strategies.

Despite broader economic headwinds, our TV division delivered strong YoY growth, up 15%, driven by the increasing adoption of OLED and Neo QLED technology. Our investments in display technology and picture quality have resonated with consumers, resulting in higher market share and premium pricing. Specifically, our OLED TV sales increased by 35% YoY, reflecting the growing demand for self-emissive display technology. The digital appliance division continued to benefit from the increasing demand for smart home solutions and energy-efficient appliances, growing 12% YoY. Our focus on innovation and design has allowed us to differentiate ourselves from competitors and capture a larger share of the market. We also expanded our distribution network in key markets, which contributed to the increased sales volume. Favorable currency exchange rates, specifically, the weakening of the Korean Won against major currencies, particularly the US dollar and the Euro, had a positive impact on our revenue. We estimate that favorable currency exchange rates contributed approximately 2 percentage points to our YoY revenue growth.

In our Q4 2023 earnings call, we provided revenue guidance of KRW 62 trillion for Q1 2024. Our actual revenue of KRW 65.4 trillion exceeded this guidance by 5.5%. This outperformance was primarily due to higher-than-expected smartphone demand. Our initial guidance was based on a more conservative estimate of demand for the Galaxy S24 series. The overwhelming positive reception to the new devices and the effective execution of our marketing campaigns resulted in significantly higher sales than anticipated. We underestimated the impact of the AI-powered features on consumer demand, particularly among early adopters and tech enthusiasts. We had anticipated a decline in TV ASPs due to competitive pressures and seasonal factors. However, the shift towards premium models and the successful launch of our new Neo QLED lineup allowed us to maintain higher ASPs than initially projected. This was also helped by our loyalty programs, which encouraged existing customers to upgrade to higher-end models. We were able to effectively manage our supply chain and avoid major disruptions, ensuring that we could meet the increased demand for our products. This was particularly important in the context of the ongoing global supply chain challenges. We had taken proactive measures to diversify our supplier base and increase our inventory levels, which allowed us to respond quickly to changes in demand.

The strong Q1 performance underscores the effectiveness of our strategic focus on innovation, product differentiation, and market expansion. We remain committed to investing in cutting-edge technologies and developing products that meet the evolving needs of our customers. Looking ahead, we anticipate continued growth in the smartphone and TV segments, driven by the increasing demand for premium products and the adoption of new technologies. We also see significant opportunities in the digital appliance and enterprise solutions markets. However, we are mindful of the potential challenges posed by the uncertain global economic environment, including inflation, rising interest rates, and geopolitical risks. We will continue to monitor these developments closely and adjust our strategies accordingly. In summary, Q1 2024 was a highly successful quarter, exceeding expectations and setting new benchmarks. We are confident that we can build on this momentum and deliver strong results for the remainder of the year. We will provide updated guidance for Q2 2024 during our next earnings call.

Now, turning to segment performance, the Semiconductor business reported a slight decrease in overall profits this quarter. While revenue remained relatively stable at $15.8 billion, a 1% decrease year-over-year, profitability was negatively impacted. The NAND flash memory market experienced a continued price decline, averaging a 7% decrease in ASP this quarter. This price erosion, driven by industry-wide oversupply, directly impacted the segment's margins. We anticipate a gradual stabilization in NAND pricing in the coming quarters as demand in enterprise storage solutions picks up, but the overall impact for the year is likely to be negative. DRAM performance remained a relative bright spot, with a 5% increase in revenue year-over-year, driven by strong demand for high-bandwidth memory (HBM) in AI and server applications. We are seeing particular strength in our DDR5 offerings, which are gaining traction in the PC and data center markets. The production disruption at our Austin fab, caused by unforeseen weather-related issues, resulted in an estimated $350 million impact on revenue and a 2% decrease in the segment's gross margin. Operations have since returned to full capacity, and we are working to recoup lost production in the coming quarter. Initial costs associated with ramping up our new memory fabs in Pyeongtaek, South Korea, also contributed to the margin decline. These costs, primarily related to equipment installation and initial production runs, amounted to approximately $180 million. We expect these costs to normalize by the end of Q1 next year, leading to improved margins in the subsequent quarters. The Semiconductor business segment experienced a gross margin of 38.5%, down from 40.2% in the previous quarter and 41% year-over-year. While the Austin fab disruption and NAND price declines presented challenges this quarter, we remain confident in the long-term growth prospects of the semiconductor market. Our investments in HBM and advanced memory technologies are positioning us for success in the high-performance computing and AI segments. We are actively managing our NAND flash production capacity to align with market demand and expect to see gradual improvements in profitability as the year progresses. We are also working to improve operational efficiency across our manufacturing footprint to mitigate the impact of future disruptions. We are actively implementing advanced packaging techniques like 2.5D and 3D integration to improve the performance and density of our memory solutions. This will allow us to deliver cutting-edge products for applications such as AI, HPC, and data centers.

Finally, I'd like to discuss our capital expenditure. Our consolidated CapEx for the first quarter of 2024 totaled KRW 9.7 trillion. This represents a slight decrease of 3% compared to the KRW 10.0 trillion spent in Q1 2023, reflecting our continued efforts to optimize capital allocation while maintaining a strong commitment to future growth. This decrease is primarily attributable to efficiency gains in our construction processes and a slight shift in the timing of certain equipment deliveries, rather than a reduction in overall investment ambition. The vast majority of our CapEx this quarter, specifically KRW 8.5 trillion, approximately 88%, was allocated to our Semiconductor division. This underlines the strategic importance of this business unit and our dedication to maintaining and extending our technology leadership. The remaining KRW 0.7 trillion, approximately 7%, was directed towards our Display business, with the remaining 5% attributed to infrastructure and R&D across the entire group. This distribution aligns with our long-term strategic goals of capturing market share in both Memory and Foundry businesses, while strategically investing in our Display technologies. A significant portion of our Memory investment, approximately KRW 3.57 trillion, was dedicated to capacity expansions at our Pyeongtaek campus in South Korea. Specifically, we're ramping up production of our latest generation DDR5 memory, leveraging advanced process nodes to improve density and energy efficiency. This is crucial to address the surging demand from data centers and high-performance computing applications. We're projecting a 15% increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year to $2.3 billion from memory sales, driven by this increased capacity and the higher ASPs associated with these advanced memory technologies. The remaining 40% of Memory CapEx, KRW 2.38 Trillion focused on advanced process migration at our Xian fab in China. This investment enables us to produce the next generation of NAND flash memory, crucial for solid-state drives, SSDs, and mobile devices. We are implementing a new 176-layer NAND architecture here, allowing us to significantly increase storage density and reduce per-bit cost. While this migration involves some short-term production adjustments, we expect to see a 12% reduction in NAND production costs by Q4 2024, giving us a significant competitive advantage. Our Foundry business continues to be a major focus for growth. The KRW 2.55 trillion investment is primarily aimed at expanding capacity for advanced processes, particularly those utilizing Extreme Ultraviolet, EUV, lithography at our facilities in South Korea and the United States. A significant portion, approximately KRW 1.79 Trillion, is dedicated to scaling up production of our 5-nanometer EUV process node. We're seeing strong demand from customers in the mobile, AI, and automotive sectors for chips manufactured using this technology. Our yield rates on the 5nm EUV process are currently exceeding 85%, which allows us to rapidly scale production to meet customer demand. We anticipate a 30% increase in Foundry revenue by the end of 2024, driven by the 5nm node. The remaining Foundry CapEx, KRW 0.76 Trillion, is allocated to preliminary investments in next-generation process technologies, including our 3nm gate-all-around, GAA, architecture. This includes acquiring new EUV equipment and establishing pilot lines for this advanced node. We are on track to begin risk production of our 3nm GAA process in the second half of 2024, solidifying our position as a technology leader in the Foundry market.

The KRW 0.7 trillion investment in our Display business is primarily focused on upgrading our OLED production lines to support increasing demand for flexible and foldable displays in the mobile and IT segments. We're also investing in improving the efficiency and yield of our QD-OLED, Quantum Dot OLED, technology for large-screen TVs, with the goal of reducing production costs and increasing market competitiveness. This investment is relatively lower than the semiconductor segment, but is a critical component of our end-to-end technology solutions that enable our overall value proposition. Our primary focus in South Korea is on expanding capacity and advancing technology at our Pyeongtaek campus. This reflects our commitment to maintaining a strong manufacturing base in our home country. We are also working closely with local suppliers to develop and integrate new technologies into our production processes. Our Xian fab remains a crucial part of our NAND flash memory production. We are committed to supporting our operations in China while adhering to all applicable regulations and trade policies. We are actively managing our supply chain to mitigate any potential disruptions. Our investments in the US are primarily focused on expanding our Foundry capacity to serve the growing demand for domestically produced semiconductors. We are working closely with the US government to secure incentives and support for our investments in this region. Our Q1 2024 CapEx demonstrates our commitment to long-term growth and technology leadership in the semiconductor and display markets. We are strategically allocating our capital to address growing demand for advanced memory and foundry technologies, while also investing in next-generation display technologies. Our investments in capacity expansion, advanced process migrations, and new equipment will enable us to maintain our competitive edge and capture market share in key segments. While mindful of macroeconomic uncertainties, we remain confident in our ability to generate strong returns on our capital investments and deliver long-term value to our shareholders. We will continue to monitor the market conditions and adjust our CapEx plans as necessary to ensure that we are making the most effective use of our resources.

I’ll now pass it over to Michael Lee to walk through the numbers in more detail.

Michael Lee, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, Alex, and hello, everyone.

Let me break it down starting with sales guidance, forecast, or trend by segment next quarter or full year. We anticipate a mixed performance in Q3, with continued strength in the Memory division offsetting projected declines in the IM (Mobile) and Display divisions. For the full year, we expect revenue growth driven primarily by the semiconductor businesses, with strategic initiatives in premium product segments across all divisions aiming to bolster profitability despite ongoing component supply challenges and fluctuating consumer demand. We are cautiously optimistic about the second half recovery in component businesses and are actively addressing risks associated with foundry capacity and mobile component shortages. We project a 18% increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year to $15.7 billion, driven by robust demand for server DRAM and enterprise SSDs. Average Selling Prices (ASPs) for DRAM are expected to increase by 8% sequentially due to tight supply conditions. NAND Flash pricing is also projected to rise, albeit at a more moderate pace of 4%, supported by increasing demand from cloud service providers and data centers. For the full year 2024, we anticipate a 22% increase year-over-year, reaching approximately $65 billion in revenue. This assumes continued strong server demand throughout the year and a gradual recovery in mobile DRAM demand in the second half. We are aggressively expanding our server DRAM capacity and are on track to begin mass production of next-generation DDR6 memory in Q4 2024, positioning us to capitalize on future demand. The increasing adoption of AI and machine learning applications is fueling demand for high-bandwidth memory (HBM) solutions. We are investing heavily in HBM development and expect to see significant revenue contributions from this segment in the coming years. We are also focusing on optimizing our manufacturing processes to improve cost competitiveness and reduce our carbon footprint. We project a 5% decrease in Q3 revenue year-over-year to $6.5 billion in System Semiconductor. While the Austin fab has resumed full manufacturing capacity, the lingering effects of the prior disruption will continue to impact System LSI production. Foundry revenue is expected to grow by 12%, driven by increased demand for our advanced process technologies (5nm and below). For the full year 2024, we expect a 8% increase year-over-year, reaching approximately $28 billion in revenue. This assumes a gradual recovery in System LSI production in the second half of the year and continued strong growth in our Foundry business. Full-fledged mass production at Pyeongtaek Line 2 will significantly expand our foundry capacity and enable us to meet growing demand from global customers. We are actively collaborating with domestic and international foundries to secure additional capacity and mitigate supply chain risks. We are also investing in the development of next-generation process technologies (3nm and below) to maintain our competitive edge in the foundry market. We are focusing on automotive semiconductors as a growth driver for System LSI, particularly in advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS) and electric vehicle (EV) applications.

Now, moving to gross margin results, QoQ changes, YoY changes with reasons, Gross margin results  v.s. guidance from last quarter with reasons, which we’ve been tracking closely. The company's gross profit demonstrated resilience in Q3 2024, reaching KRW 23.9 trillion, a slight sequential increase from KRW 23.6 trillion in Q2 2024. The consolidated gross margin landed at 36.5%, a moderate outcome. While the Information and Mobile (IM) division delivered exceptional results, exceeding expectations, declines in other key business units partially offset this positive performance, resulting in a consolidated gross margin that fell slightly short of our prior guidance. A sequential increase of approximately 1.3% (KRW 23.9 trillion vs. KRW 23.6 trillion) and a slight decrease of 0.3 percentage points from Q2 2024's 36.8%. The IM division's contribution to gross profit increased by an estimated KRW 1.8 trillion QoQ, driven by the successful launch of the Galaxy Z Fold 6 and Galaxy Z Flip 6. These new foldable devices commanded premium pricing and saw strong initial sales, particularly in North America and Europe. Additionally, a favorable product mix, with a higher proportion of high-margin flagship devices sold, contributed positively. The CE division experienced a decline in gross profit of approximately KRW 0.7 trillion QoQ. This was attributed to increased component costs, particularly for display panels, and a slowdown in demand for premium TVs in key markets like China and Europe. Promotional activities to clear inventory ahead of new model launches also impacted margins. The DS division faced continued headwinds due to the ongoing memory chip downturn. While wafer shipments saw a modest increase of 5% QoQ, average selling prices (ASPs) for DRAM remained under pressure, resulting in a decline in gross profit contribution of approximately KRW 0.5 trillion. NAND flash memory saw a slight ASP increase, but not enough to offset the DRAM weakness. The DP division remained relatively stable QoQ, with a slight increase in gross profit driven by higher OLED panel shipments for mobile devices. However, increased competition from Chinese panel manufacturers limited margin expansion. A significant increase of 12% compared to Q3 2023's KRW 21.3 trillion and an increase of 1.5 percentage points from Q3 2023's 35.0%. The IM division experienced a strong rebound compared to Q3 2023, which was impacted by supply chain disruptions and weaker consumer sentiment. The successful launch of the Galaxy S24 series earlier in the year laid a strong foundation for the foldable device launches in Q3. While still facing challenges, the DS division showed signs of recovery compared to the deep trough of Q3 2023. Increased fab utilization rates and a gradual improvement in memory chip ASPs contributed to the YoY improvement. Specifically, DRAM ASPs were up 18% YoY, albeit from a very low base. The company's strategic focus on premium products across all divisions, particularly in IM and CE, has helped to improve overall gross margins YoY. This strategy has enabled the company to command higher prices and differentiate itself from competitors. Ongoing cost optimization initiatives across the organization, including supply chain efficiencies and manufacturing process improvements, have contributed to the YoY improvement in gross margins. For example, the "Project Evergreen" initiative, focused on streamlining manufacturing processes, is estimated to have saved KRW 300 billion in Q3.

Last quarter, the company projected a consolidated gross margin of 37.0% for Q3 2024. The actual gross margin was 36.5%, falling short of guidance by 0.5 percentage points. The CE division's performance fell short of expectations due to a sharper-than-anticipated decline in demand for premium TVs in China and Europe. This was partly attributed to macroeconomic headwinds and increased competition. While the semiconductor market showed signs of improvement, the pace of recovery was slower than initially anticipated. Continued pricing pressure in the DRAM market impacted gross margins. Specifically, analysts predicted a 25% ASP increase, but the actual increase was only 18%. Unfavorable foreign exchange rate movements, particularly the strengthening of the US dollar against the Korean Won, negatively impacted gross margins by approximately 0.1 percentage points. The company had hedged a portion of its foreign exchange exposure, but not enough to fully mitigate the impact. In response to the slower-than-expected demand in the CE division, the company increased promotional activity to clear inventory, which further impacted gross margins.

Lastly, I'd like to briefly touch on Operating margin results, QoQ changes, YoY changes with reasons, Operating margin results  v.s. guidance from last quarter with reasons. This report analyzes the company’s operating margin performance for Q3 2024, comparing it to Q2 2024 (QoQ), Q3 2023 (YoY), and the guidance provided during the Q2 2024 earnings call. The company achieved a consolidated operating profit of KRW 9.4 trillion in Q3 2024. This translates to an operating margin of 18.8%, a noteworthy improvement compared to previous periods. This positive result reflects a confluence of factors detailed below. Operating profit increased from KRW 8.1 trillion in Q2 2024 to KRW 9.4 trillion in Q3 2024, representing a 16% QoQ increase. This improvement led to a 1.9 percentage point expansion in operating margin, from 16.9% in Q2 to 18.8% in Q3. Solid sales performance in the smartphone division was a primary driver. The successful launch of the "Galaxy Z Fold 6" and "Galaxy Z Flip 6" foldable phones in late Q2 continued to generate strong sales momentum into Q3. Specifically, we observed a 22% increase in premium smartphone sales, devices priced above $800, QoQ, with the foldable category contributing significantly. The MX division achieved an operating margin of 22.5% in Q3, up from 20.8% in Q2. This improvement was partially driven by a favorable product mix and effective cost management initiatives. Improved profitability in the CE division further bolstered the overall operating margin. This was largely attributable to increased demand for premium TVs, particularly Neo QLED and OLED models, coupled with efficiency gains in the manufacturing process. A strategic shift towards higher-margin home appliances, such as the "Bespoke Infinite Line" refrigerators, also contributed positively. The CE division saw its operating margin rise from 8.5% in Q2 to 10.2% in Q3. While the display division experienced weak seasonality, particularly in panel sales for mobile devices, the impact was partially mitigated by increased shipments of larger-sized OLED panels for TVs. This limited the negative impact on the overall operating margin. Panel ASP, Average Selling Price, decreased by 5% QoQ, primarily due to pricing pressures in the LCD market. The DP division's operating margin declined from 15.2% in Q2 to 13.8% in Q3. The semiconductor division faced a decline in profitability due to weaker memory chip prices and slower demand for certain application processors. This was exacerbated by increased capital expenditure related to the ramp-up of 3nm GAA, Gate-All-Around, technology. The DS division experienced a contraction in operating margin, falling from 25.1% in Q2 to 21.5% in Q3.

Operating profit increased from KRW 7.8 trillion in Q3 2023 to KRW 9.4 trillion in Q3 2024, representing a 20.5% YoY increase. This resulted in a 2.8 percentage point expansion in operating margin, from 16.0% in Q3 2023 to 18.8% in Q3 2024. Strong sales of finished products, particularly smartphones and premium TVs, were a key driver of the YoY improvement. The "Galaxy S24" series, launched in Q1 2024, continued to perform well, and the introduction of the next generation foldable devices further boosted revenue. Sales for the MX division grew by 15% YoY to reach KRW 35 Trillion. Increased utilization rates for mobile OLED panels, driven by higher demand from both internal and external customers, contributed positively to the Display division's profitability. We saw external sales of flexible OLED panels increase by 28% YoY, reflecting growing adoption of this technology by other smartphone manufacturers, particularly in the Chinese market. The company's strategic investments in AI technologies, specifically in the MX division's smartphones and the CE division's appliances, began to show increased sales. The company's AI-enabled products experienced a 15% sales increase YoY, and this figure is expected to grow. Company-wide cost optimization initiatives, including streamlining supply chains and improving manufacturing efficiencies, also contributed to the improved operating margin. We estimate that these initiatives saved approximately KRW 500 billion in operating expenses during Q3 2024. During the Q2 2024 earnings call, the company projected an operating margin of approximately 17.5% - 18.0% for Q3 2024. The actual operating margin of 18.8% exceeded the upper end of the guidance range. Demand for the new foldable smartphones proved to be stronger than initially anticipated, particularly in North America and Europe. This led to higher revenue and improved profitability in the MX division. While memory chip prices remained below peak levels, they experienced a faster-than-expected recovery during Q3, driven by increased demand from data centers and the PC market. This helped to mitigate the decline in profitability in the Semiconductor division. The company successfully negotiated favorable pricing terms with key component suppliers, helping to reduce input costs and improve overall profitability. There was a significant push for higher margin products during the quarter, and the strategy was successful. There was a much higher sales percentage of higher margin products than expected.

Now, let me hand things over to Sarah to talk about product and operational progress.

Sarah Chen, Chief Technology Officer:
Thanks, Michael.

This was a busy quarter for our teams. On the innovation front, we made meaningful advances in the Display Panel business. The Display Panel business reported a sequential decrease in earnings due to typical seasonal weakness in the mobile display market. However, on a year-over-year basis, earnings improved significantly. The mobile display sector experienced a decrease in revenue of 12% quarter-over-quarter, attributed to lower demand for smartphones during the off-season. Higher OLED utilization rates across our production facilities significantly contributed to the year-over-year earnings improvement. OLED panel sales grew by 25% year-over-year due to increased adoption in high-end smartphones and growing demand for OLED TVs. Sales of large-sized display panels for TVs and monitors remained strong, increasing by 8% year-over-year. This growth was driven by the continued popularity of premium TV models with advanced display technologies such as Quantum Dot OLED (QD-OLED). The Display Panel business achieved a gross margin of 22%, up from 18% in the same quarter last year. The higher margin was primarily driven by the increased sales of OLED panels and improved operational efficiency. The Display Panel business delivered a solid performance this quarter despite the seasonal headwinds in the mobile segment. Our investments in OLED technology are paying off, as evidenced by the significant growth in OLED panel sales. We are focused on further improving OLED utilization rates and expanding our customer base for OLED TVs. We anticipate a strong rebound in mobile display demand in the coming quarters as new smartphone models are launched. Demand for our high-resolution OLED panels is particularly strong in the Chinese market, where local smartphone manufacturers are increasingly adopting OLED displays for their premium models. We are also seeing growing demand for our automotive displays in Europe and North America.

Also worth noting is our improvement in Q1 2024 revenue, which, as Alex mentioned, exceeded guidance.

And we’ve made foundational changes in how we approach the Network Business, particularly on the fulfillment and logistics side. The Network business maintained its solid performance as 5G continues to expand globally. Revenue remained relatively stable at $4.2 billion, a 2% increase year-over-year. The continued rollout of 5G networks worldwide drove demand for our network infrastructure equipment, including base stations, core network solutions, and radio units. We are seeing strong demand for our 5G solutions in North America, where telecommunications operators are rapidly deploying 5G networks to meet the growing demand for high-speed mobile data. The Network business achieved a gross margin of 28%, consistent with the previous quarter. The Network business continues to benefit from the global expansion of 5G networks. We are focused on providing innovative and reliable network solutions to our customers, and we are committed to being a leader in the 5G market. We anticipate continued growth in the coming years as 5G networks become more widespread. We are actively developing advanced 5G technologies, such as massive MIMO and beamforming, to improve the performance and efficiency of 5G networks. We are also exploring new applications of 5G technology, such as industrial automation and smart cities.

Let’s now open the floor for questions.

Q&A SESSION

Analyst 1:
Hi, thanks for taking my question. On the Mobile Business, could you expand on what’s driving that strength?

Alex Johnson:
Certainly. The Mobile business reported significant improvements in earnings both quarter-over-quarter and year-over-year. Revenue increased by 15% year-over-year to $28.5 billion. Sales of flagship smartphone models, such as the Galaxy S23 and Z Fold series, grew considerably, contributing significantly to the revenue increase. We observed a 20% increase in sales volume for the Galaxy S23 series compared to its predecessor. Sales of mass-market smartphone models also experienced healthy growth, driven by increased demand in emerging markets such as India and Southeast Asia. Contributions from products in the Device Ecosystem lineup, including tablets, PCs, and wearables, also grew. Tablet sales increased by 10% year-over-year, driven by the success of the Galaxy Tab S8 series. Wearable device sales increased by 18% year-over-year, fueled by strong demand for our latest smartwatch models. The Mobile business achieved a gross margin of 35%, up from 32% in the same quarter last year. This improvement was driven by a favorable product mix, increased sales volume, and improved operational efficiency. The Mobile business delivered an outstanding performance this quarter, driven by strong sales of our flagship smartphones and growing contributions from our Device Ecosystem. We are focused on continuing to innovate and deliver differentiated products that meet the evolving needs of our customers. We are also committed to expanding our presence in emerging markets and strengthening our position in the premium smartphone segment. Our strategy of offering a diverse portfolio of products across different price points is proving successful. This allows us to cater to a wider range of consumers and capture market share in both developed and emerging markets.

Analyst 2:
A follow-up on Gross margin results. How confident are you that the improvements will be sustained?

Michael Lee:
Well, while we feel good about our progress, we need to be cognizant of the risks. The ongoing component shortages, particularly in the mobile and display businesses, remain a significant risk. We are actively working to diversify our supply chain and secure long-term supply agreements with key suppliers. Geopolitical tensions and trade disputes could disrupt our supply chain and impact our sales in certain markets. We are closely monitoring the geopolitical situation and are prepared to take mitigating actions as necessary. The competitive landscape in all of our business segments is becoming increasingly intense. We are focusing on differentiating our products and services through innovation, quality, and brand building.

Analyst 3:
And for Display Panel business, any update on QD-OLED adoption?

Sarah Chen:
We are actively working to increase the adoption of OLED panels in various applications, including laptops, monitors, and automotive displays. We are also investing heavily in the development of next-generation display technologies, such as microLED, to maintain our leadership position in the display market. We are focusing on expanding our partnerships with leading TV manufacturers to increase the adoption of our QD-OLED technology.

Analyst 4:
Just a final one — on the CE (Consumer Electronics) Division, is the improvement mostly due to pent-up demand?

Michael Lee:
Not entirely, although that certainly played a role. The CE Division reported strong growth in both revenue and profitability, driven by continued pent-up demand for digital appliances and expanding sales of premium TV products. Revenue increased by 10% year-over-year to $12.5 billion. Expanding sales of premium TV products, such as Neo QLED and OLED TVs, also contributed to the revenue growth. Sales of premium TVs increased by 15% year-over-year. The CE Division achieved a gross margin of 30%, up from 27% in the same quarter last year. This improvement was driven by increased sales volume and a favorable product mix. The CE Division delivered an excellent performance this quarter, driven by strong demand for our digital appliances and premium TV products. We are focused on continuing to innovate and deliver differentiated products that meet the evolving needs of our customers. We are also committed to expanding our presence in the smart home market. We are seeing particularly strong demand for our premium TV products in Europe and North America, where consumers are increasingly willing to pay more for high-quality viewing experiences. We are also experiencing rapid growth in the smart home market in Asia, where consumers are embracing connected devices to improve their convenience and comfort.

Closing

Alex Johnson:
Thank you again for joining us today. We remain confident in our long-term growth story and are committed to disciplined execution. We appreciate your continued interest and support.

Operator:

aspect_summary.Revenue results, QoQ changes, YoY change: Q1 2024 revenue reached KRW 65.4 trillion, a new all-time high. This exceeded the company's guidance of KRW 62 trillion by 5.5% due to higher-than-expected smartphone demand, especially for the Galaxy S24 series. Revenue increased 6.2% QoQ, driven by strong smartphone sales (up 8% QoQ) and a shift towards higher-end TV models, leading to a 5% ASP increase. Revenue increased 18.2% YoY, driven by robust growth in smartphones (up 22% YoY), strong TV sales (up 15% YoY) due to OLED and Neo QLED adoption, and digital appliance growth (up 12% YoY). Favorable currency exchange rates contributed approximately 2 percentage points to YoY growth.
aspect_summary.Operating margin results, QoQ changes, Y: Q3 2024 operating profit was KRW 9.4 trillion, resulting in an operating margin of 18.8%, exceeding the guided range of 17.5%-18.0%. This was driven by strong smartphone sales, especially the Galaxy Z Fold 6 and Flip 6, and improved profitability in the CE division due to premium TV demand and efficiency gains. Operating profit increased 16% QoQ (KRW 8.1 trillion to KRW 9.4 trillion) with operating margin expanding 1.9 percentage points (16.9% to 18.8%). Operating profit increased 20.5% YoY (KRW 7.8 trillion to KRW 9.4 trillion) with operating margin expanding 2.8 percentage points (16.0% to 18.8%). The YoY improvement was driven by strong finished product sales (smartphones and premium TVs), increased utilization rates for mobile OLED panels, and company-wide cost optimization initiatives. The semiconductor division experienced a decline in profitability due to weaker memory chip prices and increased capital expenditure related to the ramp-up of 3nm GAA technology.
aspect_summary.sales by segment or platforms, their res: Semiconductor business revenue was relatively stable at $15.8 billion, a 1% decrease YoY, with a gross margin of 38.5%. NAND flash memory pricing declined, impacting margins, while DRAM performance was strong, driven by HBM demand. Mobile business revenue increased 15% YoY to $28.5 billion, with a gross margin of 35%. Sales of flagship smartphones and mass-market models grew, along with contributions from the device ecosystem. CE Division revenue increased 10% YoY to $12.5 billion, with a gross margin of 30%. The increase was driven by digital appliances and premium TV products. Network business revenue was relatively stable at $4.2 billion, a 2% increase YoY, with a gross margin of 28%. The increase was driven by the global expansion of 5G networks. Display Panel business reported a sequential decrease in earnings but an improved YoY, with a gross margin of 22%. OLED panel sales grew significantly.
aspect_summary.CapEx, and the CapEx comments for this q: Consolidated CapEx for Q1 2024 totaled KRW 9.7 trillion, a 3% decrease compared to Q1 2023. KRW 8.5 trillion (88%) was allocated to the Semiconductor division, KRW 0.7 trillion (7%) to the Display business, and the remainder to infrastructure and R&D. Memory investment focused on capacity expansion at Pyeongtaek for DDR5 and advanced process migration at Xian for next-generation NAND. Foundry investment focused on expanding capacity for advanced processes, particularly EUV lithography. The investments aim to capture market share in memory and foundry businesses and strategically invest in display technologies.
aspect_summary.Gross margin results, QoQ changes, YoY c: Q3 2024 gross profit was KRW 23.9 trillion, a slight sequential increase from KRW 23.6 trillion in Q2 2024. The consolidated gross margin was 36.5%, a slight decrease of 0.3 percentage points from Q2 2024's 36.8%. The IM division's contribution to gross profit increased by an estimated KRW 1.8 trillion QoQ, while the CE division experienced a decline of approximately KRW 0.7 trillion QoQ. The DS division also faced continued headwinds. The gross margin increased 1.5 percentage points from Q3 2023's 35.0%. The company's strategic focus on premium products across all divisions has helped to improve overall gross margins YoY, as have cost optimization initiatives. The actual gross margin of 36.5% fell short of guidance by 0.5 percentage points, primarily due to a sharper-than-anticipated decline in demand for premium TVs in China and Europe and a slower-than-initially-anticipated recovery in the semiconductor market.
aspect_summary.sales guidance, forecast, or trend by se: The company anticipates mixed performance in Q3, with strength in Memory offsetting projected declines in IM (Mobile) and Display. For full year, revenue growth is expected from semiconductor businesses, with premium product initiatives aiming to bolster profitability. Q3 revenue is projected to increase 18% YoY to $15.7 billion, driven by server DRAM and enterprise SSDs. DRAM ASPs are expected to increase by 8% sequentially, with NAND pricing projected to rise by 4%. Full-year 2024 revenue is anticipated to increase 22% YoY, reaching approximately $65 billion. System Semiconductor Q3 revenue is projected to decrease 5% YoY to $6.5 billion. Foundry revenue is expected to grow by 12%. Full-year 2024 revenue is expected to increase 8% YoY, reaching approximately $28 billion.
